sections.content: When most investors think of overlooked Midwest real estate markets, they picture flat land and slow growth. Bismarck, North Dakota tells a different story. As the state capital and the second-largest city in North Dakota, Bismarck offers a stable economy, low vacancy rates, and home prices that still leave plenty of room for profit. Whether you are a wholesaler hunting for your next assignment, a flipper looking for undervalued properties, or a landlord building long-term cash flow, finding real estate deals in Bismarck ND is more achievable than you might think. If you are brand new to the game, start with our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide before diving into this local breakdown.
Bismarck ND Real Estate Market Overview

Bismarck sits on the Missouri River in south-central North Dakota and has a population of roughly 75,000 people. The city's economy is anchored by state government jobs, healthcare, agriculture, and energy. That economic diversity is a big deal for investors because it means the market does not crash when one sector struggles. Unlike oil-dependent cities such as Williston, Bismarck held steady even during the energy downturns of 2015 and 2020. Unemployment consistently runs below the national average, and the city has seen steady population growth of about 1 to 2 percent per year over the past decade.

As of 2024, the median home price in Bismarck sits around $310,000 to $330,000, which is well below national medians in comparable-sized cities. Average days on market hover between 30 and 50 days for retail listings, giving wholesalers and investors enough time to move on deals without the frenzy seen in larger metros. Rental demand is strong, with average 3-bedroom rents running between $1,200 and $1,600 per month depending on neighborhood and condition. These numbers create a realistic path to positive cash flow, especially if you acquire properties below market value.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Bismarck
Not every part of Bismarck offers the same opportunity. Knowing where to look is half the battle. Here is a quick breakdown of the top areas to target based on deal type and investment strategy.
North Bismarck: New Growth and Rental Demand

North Bismarck is one of the fastest-growing corridors in the city. New construction is pushing prices up, but pockets of older 1970s and 1980s ranches still exist where investors can buy at $180,000 to $220,000 and either flip or hold as rentals. The proximity to major employers and retail makes it attractive to long-term tenants.
South Bismarck: Flip-Friendly Inventory

South Bismarck features a mix of older neighborhoods with aging housing stock — exactly what flippers look for. Homes in areas like the Southgate and South Washington corridors often need cosmetic or moderate renovations. Investors who buy in the $140,000 to $190,000 range and spend $30,000 to $50,000 on renovations are targeting ARVs of $260,000 to $300,000. Use our free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to run your numbers before you commit to any flip.
Downtown and Near-Downtown: Long-Term Hold Potential

The areas surrounding downtown Bismarck have seen renewed interest as younger professionals move back to urban cores. Small multi-family properties, duplexes, and renovated bungalows command solid rents here. If you can find a duplex for $200,000 that generates $2,200 to $2,600 per month in combined rent, your numbers can work well as a long-term hold.

Pro Tip: Drive the streets around South Bismarck and the older North side neighborhoods on weekday mornings. Overgrown yards, boarded windows, and accumulated mail are signs of distressed sellers. Document every address and run skip tracing to find the owner's contact information. These boots-on-the-ground tactics still outperform digital lead sources in smaller markets like Bismarck.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Bismarck
Wholesale Deals

Wholesaling in Bismarck is viable, though it requires patience. The market is not oversaturated with wholesalers the way Phoenix or Atlanta might be, which means less competition for motivated seller leads. A typical wholesale deal here involves finding a distressed property worth $280,000 in ARV, locking it under contract at $155,000 to $175,000, and assigning the contract to a cash buyer for a $10,000 to $20,000 fee. Before you approach a seller, make sure you understand the numbers inside and out. Check out our guide on [wholesaling real estate for beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) for a full walkthrough of the process.
Fix and Flip Opportunities

Flipping in Bismarck works best when you keep renovation budgets tight. Labor costs in North Dakota are moderate, though finding reliable contractors can take time in a smaller city. Plan your timelines carefully — the brutal winters from November through March can add weeks to an exterior renovation. Experienced local flippers often start their projects in April and aim to list before the fall school season when buyer demand peaks. A successful flip in Bismarck typically yields $30,000 to $60,000 in gross profit on a standard cosmetic rehab.
Rental Properties and Buy-and-Hold

The buy-and-hold strategy shines in Bismarck because of the city's stable employment base and low tenant turnover. Single-family homes and small multi-family properties offer the strongest cash-on-cash returns when purchased off-market. A 3-bedroom home bought at $200,000 with 20 percent down and renting for $1,400 per month can generate $200 to $400 per month in positive cash flow after mortgage, taxes, insurance, and maintenance. That is not retirement money on its own, but scale it to five or ten doors and the picture changes dramatically.
Where to Find Off-Market Deals in Bismarck

The best real estate deals in Bismarck ND rarely show up on Zillow. Off-market properties are where the real margins live. Common sources include probate court filings, tax-delinquent property lists from Burleigh County, direct mail campaigns targeting absentee owners, and networking with local estate attorneys and property managers. Read our full breakdown on [how to find off-market real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals) to build a repeatable lead generation system for this market.

items: Pull Burleigh County tax delinquent lists from the county treasurer's office — these are public records
Check probate filings at the Burleigh County Courthouse for inherited properties with motivated heirs
Send direct mail to absentee owners with out-of-state addresses in zip codes 58501, 58503, and 58504
Network at local REIA meetings — the Bismarck-Mandan area has an active investor community
Build relationships with local estate attorneys and senior care facility administrators
Drive for dollars in South Bismarck and older North side neighborhoods to find distressed properties
Use code enforcement records to identify properties flagged for violations

sections.content: Key Market Trends Investors Should Know

Bismarck's real estate market has shown resilience through national downturns, but there are a few trends worth tracking in 2024. First, inventory remains historically low, with fewer than 300 active listings in most months. That scarcity supports prices but also makes it harder to find deals on the MLS. Second, interest rate pressure has cooled buyer demand slightly, which means more sellers are open to creative deal structures like seller financing and subject-to arrangements. Third, the city is seeing increased in-migration from larger metros like Minneapolis as remote workers seek lower costs of living — a trend that supports both rental and retail demand going forward.

The best real estate markets are not the ones everyone is talking about. They are the ones with stable jobs, growing populations, and prices that still make sense on paper. Bismarck checks all three boxes.
Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Bismarck

Investing remotely in a market like Bismarck is absolutely doable, but it requires the right infrastructure. The city is small enough that a strong local network can open most doors you need. Here is how to approach it from out of state.

items: Build a local team first: find a real estate-friendly agent, a reliable property manager, and at least two contractors before you close your first deal
Visit in person at least once before buying — a single trip to Bismarck will teach you more than weeks of online research
Learn North Dakota landlord-tenant law, which is generally landlord-friendly compared to coastal states
Plan for extreme winter weather in your maintenance budget — roof, furnace, and plumbing issues spike from December through February
Use virtual tools and AI-powered platforms to analyze deals quickly before engaging your local team on promising properties
